title: Definition of done for a crew job
when: The crew needs one shared finish line for a job: when to stop adding, when QA can pass, when the user gets the result.
inputs: the kind of output (page, script, docs)
prompt:
Goal: A short, fixed list that every task meets before done, so no worker stops early and no worker keeps polishing forever.
Steps:
1. Start from the acceptance criteria: all of them pass.
2. Add the file rules: every planned file exists, none is empty, none has TODO or lorem ipsum.
3. Add the type rules: pages pass the HTML basics (lang, title, viewport, one h1), scripts pass node --check, JSON parses.
4. Add the usage rule: the user can open or run it from the README or one obvious file, with no build or install.
5. Add the stop rule: once all lines pass, call done; extra ideas go into a note for the user, not into the files.
6. Put the list in the plan summary so every worker sees the same bar.
Quality bar:
- Each line is a fact that can be checked in the workspace.
- The list fits in six lines.
- It is the same for every task in the job.
Pitfalls:
- Done meaning "I wrote something" for the worker and "it works" for QA.
- Gold plating after the bar is met.
- A done list that only a human with a browser could check.
Verify:
- [ ] Criteria, files, type rules, usage and stop rule are all present.
- [ ] No line needs network access.
- [ ] QA can test each line with read_file or check.
- [ ] Extra ideas go to a note.
Output: A "Done means" block of four to six lines in the plan summary.

examples.input: when is the portfolio job finished?
examples.output: Done means: criteria pass, files nonempty, html basics pass, open index.html works, extras noted
